hero.headline: Flash flooding batters New York City and surrounding areas after torrential rain
hero.body:
Severe flash flooding struck New York City and the Tri-State area following torrential rainfall that overwhelmed the region's drainage systems. Streets became impassable rivers, vehicles were stranded in rising water, and emergency crews worked through the night to rescue motorists and assist residents in affected neighborhoods.

The extreme weather arrived after days of heavy smoke from Canadian wildfires and unusually high temperatures had already strained regional infrastructure and public services. A tornado watch that had been in effect for parts of New York and New Jersey expired, but flash flood warnings remained active across the northeast as water accumulated in low-lying areas and threatened subway stations.

The National Weather Service warned of continuing risks as the storm system moved through the region. Emergency responders prioritized rescuing people trapped in vehicles and providing aid to residents in flooded areas. The combination of wildfire smoke, intense heat, and now flooding has placed significant pressure on emergency services and public utilities throughout the metropolitan area.

Transportation networks experienced widespread disruption. Subway lines faced delays while major roads closed, affecting travel across the region. City officials advised residents to avoid unnecessary travel and remain alert for additional weather warnings as conditions continued to develop.

The flooding added to growing concerns about urban infrastructure's capacity to handle increasingly severe weather events. As water levels began to recede, cleanup operations commenced with crews starting to assess damage to both public infrastructure and private property. The extent of damage across the region remained under evaluation, with authorities not yet releasing comprehensive assessments or casualty reports.

Meteorologists continued monitoring the storm system as it progressed through the area. City and state officials were expected to provide updates on recovery efforts in the coming days, along with guidance on additional precautions residents should take.

This weather event marks the latest in a series of climate-related challenges affecting New York and surrounding areas. The rapid succession of environmental stressors, from air quality concerns to extreme temperatures and severe flooding, has tested both emergency response capabilities and resident preparedness.

The flash flooding underscored vulnerabilities in how the region's aging infrastructure handles extreme precipitation. Officials are expected to examine whether current systems can adequately manage the intensity and frequency of such weather events as climate patterns continue to shift.

Residents and businesses began documenting damage and filing reports with insurance companies and city agencies. The recovery process was expected to extend over several days as crews cleared debris, restored utilities, and assessed structural damage throughout the affected neighborhoods and commercial districts.

cards.headline: US Launches Eighth Night of Strikes on Iran After Soldiers Killed in Jordan
cards.body:
US military forces have conducted strikes against Iranian targets for the eighth consecutive night following the deaths of two American soldiers in Jordan, marking the first US troop fatalities from hostile fire since an April ceasefire agreement. The escalating conflict has seen both nations exchange intensive attacks over the past week, with particular focus on the strategically vital Strait of Hormuz.

The fatal attack on American personnel prompted immediate retaliation from US Central Command, which began launching strikes early Sunday. Iranian forces have responded by firing drones and missiles at US military installations in Kuwait and other locations across the Gulf region, demonstrating a commitment to sustained military action despite the costs to both sides.

The strikes have targeted extensive areas within Iran. US forces hit bridges in the southern Hormozgan province that serve as key transit routes for Bandar Abbas, Iran's main port. American aircraft also brought down a tower at Chabahar port on the Gulf of Oman, which the US military said the Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps used to coordinate attacks on vessels in the strait. Additional strikes damaged electrical infrastructure and Iranshahr airport.

The humanitarian toll has been significant. Iranian health ministry officials reported that renewed US strikes had killed at least 38 people and wounded more than 400 by Friday morning. The attacks on power infrastructure forced Iran's energy ministry to ask citizens to reduce electricity consumption as the power grid came under strain, with southern regions experiencing extreme heat compounded by damage to energy facilities.

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has retaliated against facilities across the region, targeting sites in Bahrain, Kuwait, Jordan, Oman and Qatar. Strikes on Kuwait damaged a power and desalination plant critical to the country's water supply, as approximately 90 percent of Kuwait's drinking water comes from desalination.

The renewed fighting has disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, which handled about one-fifth of the world's oil and gas supply before the conflict. While a memorandum of understanding signed last month stated the strait should remain open, both nations have interpreted the agreement differently, leading to competing plans for maritime transit. Shipping volume has drastically reduced as violence has escalated, though most vessels that continued to transit used the Iranian-designated route.

The Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps has threatened severe consequences for countries hosting US military bases if American attacks on infrastructure continue. The conflict has significantly impacted global energy markets, with US gas prices rising substantially. The average price of diesel fuel has exceeded $5 per gallon, while regular gas has approached $4, reflecting the instability caused by the dispute over the critical waterway.

cards.headline: Russia Launches One of Largest Ballistic Missile Attacks on Kyiv
cards.teaser: Russia fired ballistic missiles at Ukraine's capital for five hours in what President Zelensky called one of the most massive attacks of the war.
cards.body:
Russia carried out one of its largest ballistic missile attacks on Kyiv in a five-hour overnight raid, striking the capital with approximately 40 Iskander-M and hypersonic Zircon missiles. The assault killed at least one person and injured seven others, with fires and damage reported across the city. Air raid sirens sounded at 1:30am as residents heard explosions from both incoming missiles and air defense systems.

The attack followed Ukraine's strikes on two Russian warehouses the previous day, which killed at least eight people and injured 62. Ukraine has continued targeting Russian military and logistics infrastructure as part of its broader conflict strategy.

cards.headline: Atlantic Ocean current system faces potential collapse with global effects
cards.teaser: Research indicates a major Atlantic ocean current system is approaching a collapse point that could affect weather patterns reaching California.
cards.body:
A major Atlantic Ocean current system is approaching a critical tipping point, according to recent scientific research. The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation, which regulates climate patterns across multiple regions, is threatened by record heat and changing water temperatures in the North Atlantic.

Scientists have identified an unexpected danger: freshwater from melting ice in the Pacific Ocean is flowing into the Atlantic and disrupting the circulation system. The potential collapse of these currents could trigger significant climate and weather changes far beyond the Atlantic region, including effects reaching as far as California.

cards.headline: Britain Nationalizes British Steel Amid Chinese Ownership Dispute
cards.body:
The British government has brought British Steel into public ownership this week, ending Chinese control of the country's last remaining plant that produces virgin steel. The move has triggered strong criticism from China's government and demands for compensation from Jingye Group, the Chinese company that owned the steelmaker.

China's Ministry of Commerce expressed being "strongly dissatisfied" with the nationalization, stating the decision dealt "a severe blow to Chinese companies' confidence in investing in the UK". A ministry spokesperson told Chinese media that the UK government "forcibly took control of British Steel and subsequently nationalised the company in the name of national security, seriously undermining Jingye's legitimate rights and interests". The Chinese government has called on the UK to comply with the bilateral investment treaty between the two countries and treat Chinese companies fairly.

Jingye Group acquired British Steel for approximately 50 million pounds in 2020 after the steelmaker faced insolvency. The nationalization follows an emergency government intervention 15 months earlier, when Jingye threatened to close the Scunthorpe steelworks and eliminate 4,000 jobs. At that time, the Labour government recalled parliament to prevent the closure.

The UK government justified the takeover as necessary to protect what it called a vital domestic capability and to maintain steel production capacity at the Scunthorpe facility in Lincolnshire. Prime Minister Keir Starmer confirmed the nationalization on Thursday, stating: "British Steel is part of the fabric of our nation and a cornerstone of Britain's industrial strength. Today's decision secures the future of steelmaking in the UK, protects skilled jobs and safeguards a vital national capability."

The nationalization became possible following the Steel Industry (Nationalisation) Act 2026 receiving royal assent. This new law grants ministers authority to transfer steel businesses' shares or property into public ownership. Following the takeover, the government appointed a new leadership team focused on stabilizing the business and developing it into a "commercially sustainable, low-carbon enterprise".

The UK government has appointed an independent valuer to determine appropriate compensation for Jingye, an effort to prevent legal action under international investment treaties. Jingye has claimed in its UK accounts and social media statements that British Steel represents a valuable asset deserving substantial compensation, despite the company's earlier threat to allow it to fail.

The dispute marks the latest geopolitical tension between the UK and China. Previous disagreements include the government's decision to remove Huawei equipment from Britain's 5G networks in 2020 and the removal of China General Nuclear from the Sizewell C nuclear project in 2021 over security concerns. The nationalization decision could affect broader UK-China business relations and future foreign investment in Britain.

cards.headline: Taylor Farms expands lettuce recall to 27 states over parasite concerns
cards.teaser: The company voluntarily recalled iceberg lettuce after the CDC linked it to the spread of a diarrhea-causing parasite from a Mexican supplier.
cards.body:
Taylor Farms recalled shredded iceberg lettuce distributed across 27 states on Friday after federal health officials connected the product to a cyclospora outbreak. The contaminated lettuce came from a single supplier in central Mexico. Lettuce included in the recall was distributed as recently as Thursday.

The outbreak is expected to continue for at least two more weeks, as infections from recent exposures may still develop. Investigators are examining whether additional products may need to be recalled as the outbreak investigation expands.

cards.headline: Protesters Target Ukraine's Top General After Defense Minister Ousted
cards.teaser: Demonstrators supporting Ukraine's ousted defense minister have begun denouncing General Oleksandr Syrskyi, the commander he clashed with in office.
cards.body:
Ukraine's top general has become a target of protester anger following the abrupt dismissal of Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov. Demonstrators have turned their focus to General Oleksandr Syrskyi, the military commander with whom Fedorov reportedly clashed while in office.

Fedorov, celebrated for his innovative, tech-driven approach to the war, had championed a strategy leveraging Ukraine's advances in drone and missile technology. His sudden removal by President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has startled European officials and sparked rare public dissent directed at Ukraine's military leadership during wartime, even as Kyiv appeared to be gaining advantages across multiple fronts.

cards.headline: Ferry Carrying 116 Passengers Sinks Off Guyana Coast
cards.teaser: A ferry capsized between Georgetown and Port Kaituma with 116 people on board, authorities said.
cards.body:
A passenger ferry sank off the coast of Guyana with 116 people aboard, according to authorities. The vessel capsized while traveling between Georgetown and Port Kaituma, prompting a rescue operation.

Rescue teams have pulled 53 people from the water so far. Authorities continue to search for the remaining passengers. The cause of the capsizing has not been determined.

cards.headline: Hungary's President Signs Amendment Ending His Own Term
cards.teaser: Hungarian President Tamás Sulyok signed a constitutional amendment that terminates his own mandate.
cards.body:
Hungary's President Tamás Sulyok has stepped down after signing a constitutional amendment passed by parliament's ruling Tisza party, led by Prime Minister Péter Magyar. The amendment ended his term immediately, citing society's "serious loss of confidence" in his leadership.

Sulyok was elected in early 2024 by lawmakers from former Prime Minister Viktor Orbán's Fidesz party. His removal reflects shifting political dynamics in Budapest's government leadership.

cards.headline: Tate Brothers Arrested in US, Face Extradition to UK
cards.teaser: The Crown Prosecution Service requested the extradition of the Tate brothers from the United States as UK charges against them reached 59.
cards.body:
The Tate brothers were arrested in Miami after British prosecutors requested their extradition. The Crown Prosecution Service has brought 59 charges against them, including rape and trafficking offenses. The brothers were taken into custody on a sealed warrant, according to the US Marshals Service.

A lawyer representing the brothers maintains their innocence. UK and US authorities are coordinating on the extradition process.

cards.headline: Cuban Dissident Luis Manuel Otero Alcántara Goes Into Exile in US
cards.teaser: The artist and activist, who spent five years in prison after Cuba's largest anti-government protests in decades, has arrived in the United States.
cards.body:
Cuban dissident artist Luis Manuel Otero Alcántara has been granted permission to travel to the United States after his prison sentence ended in July. He was arrested in 2021 during Cuba's largest anti-government protests in decades and sentenced to five years in prison in 2022 on charges of insulting national symbols, contempt, and disturbing the public order.

Amnesty International designated Otero Alcántara as a prisoner of conscience. His whereabouts had remained unknown following the conclusion of his prison term until his official Facebook page announced he had been cleared to leave Cuba.

cards.headline: US strikes Iranian Revolutionary Guard following attack that killed troops in Jordan
cards.teaser: The United States launched military strikes against Iranian Revolutionary Guard forces after an attack in Jordan killed two American service members.
cards.body:
The US military conducted strikes against Iranian Revolutionary Guard forces for the eighth consecutive night following an attack that killed two American service members in Jordan. Iran responded by firing drones at US military positions in Kuwait, escalating the exchange of military action between the two countries.

The strikes represent a significant escalation in US-Iran tensions, with American forces directly targeting Iranian sites in response to the deaths of American personnel in the region.

cards.headline: Andrew and Tristan Tate arrested in Miami as UK files 59 charges
cards.teaser: US Marshals arrested social media influencers Andrew and Tristan Tate in Miami after the UK Crown Prosecution Service requested their extradition on rape and sex trafficking charges.
cards.body:
US Marshals arrested Andrew and Tristan Tate in Miami following an extradition request from the United Kingdom. The Crown Prosecution Service has filed 59 charges against the brothers, including rape and sex trafficking offenses.

British prosecutors are seeking the brothers' extradition to face trial in the UK. Their lawyer has stated they are innocent of all charges.

cards.headline: Russia launches large-scale ballistic missile attack on Kyiv
cards.teaser: Russia fired 41 missiles and 125 attack drones across Ukraine overnight, with President Zelensky describing it as one of the most massive ballistic attacks on the capital.
cards.body:
Russia carried out one of its largest-ever ballistic missile attacks on Kyiv overnight, launching approximately 40 Iskander-M and hypersonic Zircon missiles in a five-hour assault. The bombardment began around 1:30am, with air defense systems engaging incoming fire throughout the night. At least one person was killed and seven others injured in the strikes, with fires and building damage reported across the capital.

President Volodymyr Zelensky described the attack as one of the most massive ballistic assaults on Ukraine's capital since the war began. The strike represents a significant escalation in Russia's aerial campaign targeting Ukrainian cities and infrastructure.

cards.headline: Spain faces Argentina in World Cup final with Lamine Yamal seeking defining moment
cards.teaser: The World Cup final will determine how Lamine Yamal's tournament performance is remembered, despite the Spanish player having a less prominent showing than expected.
cards.body:
Spain and Argentina will meet in the World Cup final on Sunday, featuring two of football's biggest stars. Lionel Messi will make his 34th World Cup appearance for Argentina, potentially his last in the tournament. For Spain's Lamine Yamal, a championship would reshape how his World Cup performance is remembered after a quiet tournament.

The final has taken on added significance beyond the pitch. Racist incidents involving some Argentina fans have prompted criticism from across Latin America, with prominent voices expressing reluctance to support the South American team despite regional solidarity.

cards.headline: Andy Burnham to replace Keir Starmer as UK Prime Minister
cards.teaser: Andy Burnham will become Prime Minister following a meeting with King Charles III, as his spokesperson announces plans to scrap digital ID proposals.
cards.body:
Andy Burnham will replace Sir Keir Starmer as Prime Minister after meeting with King Charles III. The transition marks a change in Labour leadership at the top of government. Burnham's deputy indicated the incoming leader will pursue bolder policies while adhering to the Labour manifesto.

In his first major policy announcement, a spokesperson for Burnham confirmed the government will scrap plans for a digital identification system. The spokesperson said the new administration would focus its efforts where people need support most urgently. The digital ID plan had been a point of debate within political circles regarding privacy and government surveillance.

cards.headline: Israeli paraglider works to protect swifts nesting at Western Wall
cards.teaser: An Israeli paraglider has taken on efforts to save swifts that have nested in Jerusalem's Western Wall since ancient times.
cards.body:
Swifts have nested in Jerusalem's Western Wall since biblical times, making the birds part of this sacred site's long history. One Israeli paraglider has taken on the mission of protecting these migrating birds and their nesting habitat at the wall.

The conservation effort aims to preserve the swifts' ability to return to the Western Wall each season, maintaining a tradition that connects modern Jerusalem to its ancient past.

cards.headline: Chinese AI Company Moonshot Plans IPO Within Six Months
cards.teaser: Moonshot AI announced plans to go public following a breakthrough with its Kimi language model.
cards.body:
Moonshot AI, a Chinese artificial intelligence company, plans to launch an initial public offering within six months. The company has unveiled its Kimi K3 model, which it claims can compete with leading American AI firms.

The development has drawn attention from US technology officials concerned about America's position in global AI competition. OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic have led American advances in artificial intelligence, but Moonshot's progress with Kimi represents an emerging challenge to that dominance.

cards.headline: Apple Sues OpenAI and Sends Legal Letters to Employees
cards.teaser: Apple filed a lawsuit against OpenAI and contacted dozens of OpenAI employees with legal correspondence.
cards.body:
Apple has initiated legal action against OpenAI and sent legal letters to dozens of OpenAI employees, according to reports. The lawsuit marks an escalation in tensions between the iPhone maker and the ChatGPT developer as competition intensifies in the artificial intelligence sector.

The dispute centers on AI technology development and potential intellectual property issues. Apple has been developing its own AI capabilities while OpenAI has emerged as a leader in generative AI. The legal letters to OpenAI employees suggest Apple may be concerned about talent recruitment or trade secrets.

cards.headline: Incoming British PM Expected to Announce North Sea Oil Support
cards.teaser: Prime Minister Burnham is anticipated to pledge new backing for North Sea energy production from the first day in office.
cards.body:
Britain's incoming Prime Minister is expected to announce fresh support for the North Sea from day one of his premiership. The move signals continued government backing for oil and gas operations in British waters.

North Sea production has long been central to the UK's energy supply, though it faces ongoing scrutiny regarding climate commitments and taxation policy.

cards.headline: Taylor Farms Lettuce Tests Positive for Cyclospora Parasite
cards.teaser: A lettuce sample from Taylor Farms showed the presence of Cyclospora as the recall expands across suppliers.
cards.body:
Taylor Farms recalled shredded iceberg lettuce distributed across 27 states after testing positive for Cyclospora, a parasite causing intestinal illness. The contaminated products reached consumers as recently as Thursday, prompting immediate action from the company and affected retailers.

Health officials warn the outbreak will likely continue for at least two weeks, as infections from recent exposure cases continue to emerge. The investigation may identify additional contaminated products in the coming days as authorities work to determine the full scope of contamination.

cards.headline: New EU Border System Causing Extended Passport Control Delays
cards.teaser: A new European Union border control system is tripling processing times at airports, according to aviation officials.
cards.body:
The European Union's new border system is causing passport control times to triple at airports, according to an airport executive. The delays affect travelers entering EU countries and have prompted warnings from airlines about extended waits.

Ryanair has advised passengers traveling to Europe to prepare for longer processing times at border checkpoints. The new system represents a change in how the EU processes entry documentation for international travelers.

cards.headline: Prediction Market Founders Polymarket and Kalshi Locked in Rivalry
cards.teaser: The young billionaire founders of competing prediction platforms Polymarket and Kalshi are engaged in an intense business rivalry.
cards.body:
Shayne Coplan of Polymarket and Tarek Mansour of Kalshi, both young billionaires, are competing to dominate the prediction markets industry. The rivalry between the two founders has intensified as their platforms vie for market share.

Prediction markets allow users to bet on the outcomes of future events, from elections to economic indicators. Both Polymarket and Kalshi have attracted significant user bases and investment as the sector grows.

hero.headline: Apple raises prices for Music and One subscription services
hero.body:
Apple has increased subscription prices for Apple Music and Apple One, marking the first adjustment to Apple Music pricing since 2022. The changes affect multiple subscription tiers and will impact millions of subscribers worldwide.

The price increases apply to both individual and family plans for Apple Music. Apple One, which bundles Music with TV+, iCloud storage, and other services, has also seen price adjustments. The company simultaneously raised prices for iCloud+ storage subscriptions in several countries, with tiered plans ranging from basic to premium options.

Apple has not disclosed the specific percentage increases or provided detailed reasoning for the adjustments. However, the timing coincides with broader industry challenges. The company recently explained that rising memory and storage chip costs, driven by demand from the AI industry's data center expansion, have forced it to raise prices on multiple products.

"We have never seen a component price increase this much, this quickly," Apple stated when announcing price hikes for iPads and MacBooks. The company said it had previously shielded customers from these increases but has now reached a point where price adjustments are necessary.

Memory chip prices have surged dramatically. Dynamic random access memory costs rose as much as 98% in the first quarter of 2026 and are expected to jump another 58% to 63% in the current quarter, according to industry tracker TrendForce. AI chipmakers like Nvidia have signed long-term deals with memory manufacturers, prioritizing their orders over consumer electronics companies.

Even with Apple's renowned supply chain relationships, the company cannot completely absorb these costs. Competitors like Dell have faced even steeper price increases. Micron, a major memory supplier, has locked in $22 billion in long-term commitments from customers seeking to secure their memory supplies.

This pricing pressure extends across the tech industry. Research firm IDC estimates the smartphone market will experience its biggest-ever annual decline of nearly 14% this year, while the PC market is expected to fall 11.3%.

Industry analysts expect iPhone prices will increase next. Nabila Popal, senior research director at IDC, noted that Apple strategically announced these price hikes before the iPhone launch to ensure headlines focus on new features rather than cost increases.

New subscribers and existing customers will transition to the updated pricing at their next billing cycle, which begins next month. Apple Music competes with Spotify and Amazon Music in the streaming market. The subscription price adjustment represents a significant shift after the company maintained its pricing structure for roughly four years.

cards.headline: Lego adds chips to bricks in push beyond screens
cards.teaser: The toy maker is embedding technology into its physical building blocks as part of a strategy to compete with digital entertainment.
cards.body:
Lego is incorporating computer chips into its brick products as the company works to maintain relevance against screen-based entertainment. The move represents a shift in how the traditional toy maker approaches product development in a digital age.

The chip-enabled bricks aim to blend physical play with technological features. Lego faces increasing competition from video games, apps, and other digital entertainment options that have drawn children away from traditional toys. The company views the integration of technology into its core product line as a way to offer interactive experiences while preserving hands-on building play.

cards.headline: Waymo resumes San Francisco autonomous vehicle service after one-hour pause
cards.teaser: The self-driving car company halted operations briefly due to power outages affecting its systems.
cards.body:
Waymo resumed its autonomous vehicle service in San Francisco after pausing operations for approximately one hour. The company experienced disruptions that required a temporary halt to its robotaxi fleet in the city.

Power outages caused the service interruption, affecting Waymo's ability to operate its self-driving vehicles. This marks another instance of infrastructure issues impacting the company's autonomous transportation service. Waymo has previously encountered operational challenges related to power and connectivity problems in its service areas.

cards.headline: NASA Psyche mission releases Mars flyby data and time-lapse footage
cards.teaser: The spacecraft captured surface details and imagery during its pass by the red planet.
cards.body:
NASA's Psyche mission delivered data and time-lapse video from its Mars flyby. The spacecraft collected information about the Martian surface and captured images showing the growing crescent of Mars as the mission approached the planet.

The mission tested a gamma-ray sensor built by Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory during the flyby. Psyche captured detailed views of Martian surface features as part of its journey. The spacecraft is ultimately bound for the metallic asteroid Psyche in the main asteroid belt, using Mars as a gravity assist and testing opportunity for its scientific instruments.

cards.headline: Perseid meteor shower begins five-week display
cards.teaser: One of the year's most active meteor showers started this weekend and will continue into August.
cards.body:
The Perseid meteor shower began lighting up night skies and will remain visible for the next five weeks. The annual event ranks among the most active meteor showers observable from Earth each year.

The Perseids occur when Earth passes through debris left by the Swift-Tuttle comet. Observers can expect to see increasing meteor activity as the shower builds toward its peak in the coming weeks. The display will be visible across the Northern Hemisphere under clear, dark sky conditions.

cards.headline: iPhone 18 Pro details emerge ahead of expected September launch
cards.teaser: Leaked information and diagnostics logs point to camera specifications and features for Apple's next flagship phone.
cards.body:
Details about the iPhone 18 Pro have surfaced through leaked diagnostics logs and industry reports. The information reveals camera specifications and suggests the device will launch in approximately two months, following Apple's established event timeline pattern.

The iPhone 18 Pro models are expected to feature 12 new capabilities compared to current versions. Leaked specifications indicate changes to camera systems, with the Pro Max variant receiving particular attention. Reports suggest the new models will be larger and heavier than their predecessors, with enhanced camera hardware as a primary upgrade focus.

hero.headline: Kylian Mbappé breaks World Cup goal-scoring record with 22 career goals
hero.body:
Kylian Mbappé has become the World Cup's all-time leading scorer after netting two goals in France's third-place match against a rival team. The French forward now holds the record with 22 goals across World Cup tournaments, surpassing the previous mark held by Lionel Messi.

The 27-year-old achieved this milestone in the consolation game following France's semifinal exit from the 2026 tournament. Mbappé's two goals in the match pushed him past Messi, who had held the record and advanced to the World Cup final to represent Argentina.

Multiple major outlets including ESPN and Yahoo Sports confirmed the new scoring record, highlighting the significance of Mbappé's achievement. The milestone represents another notable accomplishment for the French captain, who has consistently performed on international football's biggest stage throughout his career.

Mbappé's path to the record demonstrates his scoring ability across multiple World Cup tournaments. His consistent performance in crucial matches has established him among the sport's most prolific international goal scorers. The record now stands as a benchmark for future players competing in the tournament.

Despite breaking the all-time record, Mbappé acknowledged Messi's continued presence in the tournament. According to reports from Yahoo Sports, Mbappé discussed why he believes the Argentine captain could still win the 2026 World Cup Golden Boot, the award given to the tournament's top scorer. Messi retains the opportunity to add to his goal tally in the final match against Spain.

The record marks another individual achievement for French football, even as the team fell short of reaching consecutive World Cup finals. France's semifinal elimination prevented them from securing back-to-back appearances in the championship match. However, Mbappé's personal success provides a bright spot for the nation after their tournament disappointment.

Messi, who turned 39 on Wednesday, made history of his own earlier in the tournament. He broke the previous World Cup goal-scoring record with a clinical finish against Austria in a group stage match. The moment held particular significance as it occurred in Dallas, in the same city where Maradona was forced to leave the 1994 World Cup under controversy, and exactly 40 years after Maradona's infamous hand-of-God goal against England.

The Argentine captain has now faced setbacks during his World Cup journey, including missing a penalty against Austria before ultimately recording his historic goals. His performance throughout the tournament has kept him in contention for the Golden Boot award as Argentina prepares for the final against Spain.

Both records underscore the remarkable goal-scoring prowess displayed during this World Cup tournament, with two of football's greatest players etching their names further into the sport's history books.

cards.headline: Lionel Messi to play 34th World Cup match in final
cards.teaser: The Argentina captain will set a new appearance record in the World Cup final, with questions surrounding whether it will be his last tournament game.
cards.body:
Lionel Messi will make his 34th World Cup appearance when Argentina faces Spain in the final, extending his record for most World Cup matches played. At 39 years old, the Argentine captain has the chance to win his second World Cup title, having led his country to victory in 2022.

The final brings together two of football's transcendent stars in Messi and Spain's Lamine Yamal. However, the match has become a charged topic across Latin America, with some supporters conflicted about which team to back due to racial incidents involving Argentine fans during the tournament.

cards.headline: Dricus du Plessis defeats Kamaru Usman at UFC Oklahoma City
cards.teaser: The South African fighter dominated the former welterweight champion in a one-sided decision victory in the main event.
cards.body:
Dricus du Plessis secured a decisive points victory over Kamaru Usman in the UFC Oklahoma City main event. The South African middleweight controlled the fight from start to finish, overwhelming Usman throughout the contest.

ESPN described the bout as one-sided, with du Plessis picking apart the former UFC welterweight champion. The victory strengthens du Plessis's position in the middleweight division. Usman, who had moved up in weight, was unable to match du Plessis's pace and pressure during the fight.

cards.headline: Josh Kerr suggests he could attempt to break mile world record
cards.teaser: The British middle-distance runner said setting a new mile record would be an awesome achievement and hinted at a possible attempt.
cards.body:
Josh Kerr shattered the men's mile world record in London on Saturday, running 3 minutes 42.66 seconds. The British runner surpassed Morocco's Hicham El Guerrouj's 27-year-old record by 0.47 seconds.

Kerr had publicly announced his intention to break the record months in advance. By delivering on his promise at the Diamond League meet, he became the seventh British man to hold the mile world record.

cards.headline: Bukayo Saka's hat-trick against France intensifies England selection debate
cards.teaser: The winger's three-goal performance has raised questions about Thomas Tuchel's decision to leave him out of the semifinal.
cards.body:
Bukayo Saka scored a hat-trick as England defeated France 6-4 in the World Cup third-place playoff at Miami Stadium, securing their best men's World Cup finish since 1966. Captain Declan Rice had given England an early lead with a goal in the third minute.

Saka's standout performance has reignited debate over Thomas Tuchel's decision to exclude him from the semifinal lineup. The Arsenal winger's three-goal display demonstrated his attacking prowess on the tournament stage, prompting scrutiny of the England manager's tactical selections during the competition.

cards.headline: Argentina rugby coach Felipe Contepomi walks out of news conference after England loss
cards.teaser: The head coach left his media appearance following Argentina's 31-24 defeat to England in the Nations Championship.
cards.body:
Felipe Contepomi walked out of his post-match news conference after Argentina's 31-24 loss to England in the Nations Championship. The Argentine head coach departed the media session without completing his scheduled appearance.

Contepomi accused England of showing a lack of respect following the defeat in Santiago.

cards.headline: Wales rugby finishes season with three wins and nine defeats
cards.teaser: Steve Tandy's first season as head coach concluded with a loss in Durban, capping a difficult campaign for the national team.
cards.body:
Wales completed Steve Tandy's debut season as head coach with a record of three wins and nine defeats across 12 international matches. The team's performance in Durban marked the final game of a season that raised questions about the program's direction.

The Welsh rugby team struggled throughout Tandy's first year in charge. BBC Sport reported mounting questions for Wales following the Durban defeat, with the poor record prompting scrutiny of the team's development under the new coaching staff.

hero.headline: Jennifer Finch, L7 Bassist, Dies at 59
hero.body:
Jennifer Finch, bassist and founding member of the influential rock band L7, has died at age 59. Finch had been diagnosed with an aggressive form of brain cancer.

Finch co-founded L7 in Los Angeles in 1985, helping establish the band as a pioneering force in the grunge and alternative rock movements of the late 1980s and 1990s. The all-female group became known for their aggressive sound and confrontational stage presence, releasing seven studio albums over their career. L7's music addressed social and political issues while challenging gender norms in the male-dominated rock scene of the era.

The bassist played a central role in L7's most successful period, which included the albums "Bricks Are Heavy" in 1992 and "Hungry for Stink" in 1994. The band's single "Pretend We're Dead" became a mainstream hit and remains one of the defining songs of the grunge era. Beyond her work with L7, Finch was an active participant in the Rock for Choice benefit concert series, which raised funds and awareness for reproductive rights throughout the 1990s.

Finch's musical career extended beyond L7. She played bass for the punk band The Runaways during a brief stint in 1987 and collaborated with numerous other artists in the alternative rock community. After L7 initially disbanded in 2001, Finch continued working in music and appeared on various recording projects. The band reunited in 2014 and had been performing sporadically in recent years.

Finch's death represents the loss of a significant figure in alternative rock history. Her contributions to L7 helped pave the way for future generations of women in rock music. The band's influence continues to be felt in contemporary punk and alternative music, with many artists citing L7 as an inspiration for their own work.

cards.headline: Andrew and Tristan Tate Arrested in Miami
cards.teaser: Social media influencers Andrew and Tristan Tate were arrested by federal officers in Miami, though charges were not immediately disclosed.
cards.body:
Andrew and Tristan Tate were arrested by federal officers in Miami on Saturday afternoon on a sealed warrant, according to the U.S. Marshals Service. This represents the second major arrest for the brothers, who were previously detained in Romania in 2022 by anti-terrorism authorities.

British prosecutors have requested the extradition of the brothers from the U.S. on rape and trafficking charges. The Crown Prosecution Service has brought a total of 59 charges against them. Their lawyer has stated they are innocent. The Tate brothers have built large social media followings, with Andrew Tate known for promoting content about masculinity and wealth.

cards.headline: Christopher Nolan Says Next Film at Least Three Years Away After 'The Odyssey'
cards.teaser: Director Christopher Nolan said he will take at least three years before making another film after completing work on The Odyssey.
cards.body:
Christopher Nolan told Today that he won't make another film for at least three years following The Odyssey. The ambitious adaptation of Homer's epic poem, which reportedly cost $250 million, took a significant physical and creative toll on the director.

In an interview at the film's London premiere, Nolan acknowledged the grueling nature of the project. He described experiencing "sheer terror" ahead of the film's release, noting the enormous stakes of bringing such an expansive story to the screen. The scope and challenge of adapting the classic work proved demanding even for one of cinema's most accomplished directors.

cards.headline: Bruno Mars Returns to Wembley Stadium After Eight Years
cards.teaser: Bruno Mars performed at Wembley Stadium for the first time in eight years, delivering a performance centered on his catalog of hits.
cards.body:
Bruno Mars returned to Wembley Stadium for a performance after an eight-year absence from UK stages. The concert featured a polished production centered on his collection of hit songs.

Wembley Stadium, one of the United Kingdom's largest concert venues, provided the backdrop for this highly anticipated comeback show.

cards.headline: Author Dave Eggers Criticizes ChatGPT in Visit to OpenAI Headquarters
cards.teaser: Writer Dave Eggers told OpenAI staff that ChatGPT is silencing an entire generation during a visit to the company's offices.
cards.body:
Sam Altman invited Dave Eggers to speak with approximately 200 OpenAI staff members at the company's headquarters. Eggers, a prolific novelist and screenwriter who founded McSweeney's literary magazine and established schools and nonprofits supporting writers and the arts, argued that ChatGPT is silencing an entire generation.

His remarks reflect ongoing concerns within the literary community about generative AI's impact on creative writing and expression. Eggers has been a vocal critic of AI-generated writing and its effects on literature.

cards.headline: Malaysia International Film Festival Opens Ninth Edition in Kuala Lumpur
cards.teaser: The ninth Malaysia International Film Festival opened with a red carpet ceremony, earning official recognition from ASEAN Records.
cards.body:
The Malaysia International Film Festival launched its ninth edition on July 18 at MyTown Shopping Centre in Kuala Lumpur. The festival received official recognition from ASEAN Records during the opening ceremonies.

The eight-day event showcases international cinema, drawing filmmakers, industry leaders, and actors to the opening night festivities. Festival founder and president Joanne Goh attended the ceremony.

cards.headline: NBA Star Karl-Anthony Towns Appears at WWE Saturday Night's Main Event
cards.teaser: NBA champion Karl-Anthony Towns helped wrestler Danhausen defeat JD McDonagh at a WWE Saturday Night's Main Event taping.
cards.body:
Karl-Anthony Towns made a surprise appearance at WWE's Saturday Night's Main Event, where he assisted wrestler Danhausen in a match against JD McDonagh. The New York Knicks star helped Danhausen secure victory during the event.

The crossover appearance was part of an entertaining blend of professional basketball and wrestling, featuring Towns in support of the WWE performer.

hero.headline: Voters voice frustration with Trump's handling of Iran conflict
hero.teaser: Americans have expressed growing frustration with President Trump's approach to the war with Iran as the situation continues to shift.
hero.body:
Americans are struggling to keep pace with the rapidly shifting developments in President Trump's war with Iran, according to public feedback on the administration's handling of the conflict.

The situation in the Middle East has become increasingly complex, with multiple fronts and competing claims creating confusion among the public. The conflict extends beyond Iran itself, with significant spillover effects in neighboring regions.

One major point of confusion has centered on ceasefire agreements and their scope. Pakistan's prime minister, who served as a mediator, initially stated that a two-week ceasefire deal announced on Tuesday applied "everywhere including Lebanon and elsewhere." However, the Trump administration and Israel later contradicted this, with the White House press secretary declaring that Lebanon was not part of the agreement. Vice President JD Vance told reporters the US never promised to include Lebanon in the ceasefire. Iran has insisted Lebanon is covered, while France and Australia have urged the same interpretation.

The disagreement has had real consequences. Despite the ceasefire announcement, Israel launched what officials described as its biggest attack on Lebanon in the war on Wednesday, killing at least 254 people according to Lebanese sources. Hezbollah responded by firing rockets at northern Israel, describing the strikes as ceasefire violations.

The humanitarian toll continues to mount. The United Nations reports that 1.1 million Lebanese have been displaced since early March, representing nearly one-fifth of the country's population. That number is expected to rise following Wednesday's strikes. Israeli orders for civilians to leave now affect 15.5 percent of Lebanon's territory. The conflict has also damaged critical infrastructure, including the last remaining bridge connecting southern Lebanon to the rest of the country.

Control of the Strait of Hormuz remains a central objective. Iran announced it would temporarily reopen the vital waterway as part of the ceasefire but has now identified alternative shipping routes, citing risks from sea mines. Independent maritime analysts found no evidence of increased traffic through the strait despite White House claims, with only 11 vessels transiting on Wednesday. Iran's Revolutionary Guards have required ships to coordinate safe passage and pay substantial tolls in cryptocurrency.

The layering of different announcements, reversals, and competing claims about what the ceasefire actually covers has left many Americans struggling to understand the current situation. The rapid shifts in military operations, conflicting statements from different officials about which countries are included in agreements, and expanding humanitarian crises have made it difficult for the public to form a coherent understanding of where the conflict is headed or what the administration's actual strategy might be.

cards.headline: U.S. launches airstrikes against Iran after two troops killed in Jordan
cards.teaser: The U.S.
cards.body:
The U.S. military conducted retaliatory airstrikes against Iran on Saturday evening following an Iranian ballistic missile attack on the Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan. Two American service members were killed and others wounded in the Iranian attack, marking the first U.S. combat deaths since fighting intensified two weeks ago.

The strikes represent an escalation in U.S.-Iran hostilities. U.S. forces have now targeted Iranian sites for the eighth consecutive night, while Iran has responded with drone attacks on U.S. military positions in Kuwait. The cycle of exchanges underscores the deepening tensions between Washington and Tehran in the Middle East.

cards.headline: Trump revives election interference claims in primetime address
cards.teaser: President Trump alleged that China obtained hundreds of millions of U.S. voter records during a Thursday night speech focused on election security.
cards.body:
President Trump claimed during a primetime address on Thursday that China allegedly obtained hundreds of millions of U.S. voter records while seeking to interfere in American elections. The speech came as lawmakers consider the fallout from his push to overhaul the nation's voting system.

Trump used the address to promote the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act, legislation he is pressing Congress to approve. The speech raised alarms among observers and prompted discussions about foreign interference in U.S. elections. Lawmakers are now weighing the implications of Trump's renewed focus on election security measures and his claims about foreign access to voter information.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary orders testosterone testing for troops over 30
cards.teaser: Pete Hegseth issued a directive requiring testosterone level testing as part of periodic health assessments for service members, drawing criticism from medical experts.
cards.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth this week mandated that troops over 30 undergo testosterone level testing as part of the military's periodic health assessment. Hegseth argued the effort will ensure the optimal performance and long-term health of warfighters.

Medical experts questioned the rationale behind Hegseth's directive. The move has generated significant debate about the necessity and implications of mandatory hormone testing for military personnel. Critics raised concerns about the medical justification for the testing program and its potential impact on service members.

cards.headline: Republicans split over Trump's election overhaul push ahead of midterms
cards.teaser: President Trump's efforts to win congressional approval of election legislation are frustrating Republicans concerned about midterm prospects.
cards.body:
President Trump's push to secure congressional approval of the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act at all costs is frustrating Republicans who believe he is picking the wrong fights ahead of midterm elections. The frustrations intensified following the primetime address Trump delivered Thursday night that revisited his complaints about election security.

Republicans wary of the upcoming midterm elections expressed concern that Trump's focus on election overhaul legislation could damage the party's electoral prospects. GOP members voiced unease about the president's priorities and the timing of his push for voting system changes as the party prepares for congressional races.

cards.headline: Senator Ossoff intensifies criticism of Trump on election issues
cards.teaser: Georgia Senator Jon Ossoff has emerged as one of the Democratic Party's most vocal critics of President Trump on election matters.
cards.body:
Senator Jon Ossoff is taking an offensive posture against President Trump, establishing himself as one of the Democratic Party's most aggressive critics on elections. The Georgia Democrat won his Senate seat in a runoff election held on Jan. 5, 2021, one day before the Capitol riot.

Ossoff's heightened criticism comes amid growing speculation about his presidential ambitions. The senator has made election issues central to his political positioning, leveraging his personal experience winning a closely watched Georgia runoff to build credibility on voting matters.

cards.headline: White House defends Argentina over Falklands territorial claim display
cards.teaser: A White House official backed Argentina after its soccer team displayed a banner asserting territorial claims to the Falkland Islands following a win over England.
cards.body:
After Argentina's 2-1 World Cup semi-final victory over England in Atlanta, some players displayed a banner reading "Las Malvinas son Argentinas," asserting Argentina's claim to the Falkland Islands. The White House's FIFA task force chief defended the players' action, citing the U.S. belief in free speech.

The incident has drawn criticism from the UK, with Downing Street calling for FIFA to investigate. The banner display reignited tensions over the long-disputed islands, a persistent source of friction between Argentina and Britain.
